title: Generics Basics
description: Learn how to use generics for reusable type-safe code.

data.text: **Generics** allow you to write reusable code that works with multiple types while maintaining type safety. They're like type parameters.

data.title: Generic Function
Generic Interface

terms.definition: A placeholder for a type, like <T>
The actual type passed to a generic, like <User>
Limits what types can be used with a generic

data.title: Naming Conventions
data.text: Use T for the first type, U for the second, etc. For more descriptive names, use TResponse, TData, etc.

data.caption: Generic type flow from parameter to return
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Call: firstElement([1,2,3])] --> B[Infer T=number]
    B --> C[Return: number | undefined]
    D[Call: firstElement(['a','b'])] --> E[Infer T=string]
    E --> F[Return: string | undefined]

data.title: Exercise: Generic Identity Function
data.description: Create a generic identity function that returns its argument.
steps: Test with number, string, and object arguments
Verify TypeScript infers the return type correctly
data.expectedOutcome: A generic function that preserves the exact type of its input.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use T, U, V for generic names
data.takeaway: Generics are essential for reusable type-safe code.
